items.problem: Migrated window renders visually blank (solid white client area; only caption buttons paint) despite a complete UIA tree and a clean build. Dominant defect; drove score to 0.
items.evidence: discrepancies.json (severity=critical, type=blank-render); migration-score.json features[0].verdict=fail, note 'renders VISUALLY BLANK'; MainWindow.xaml lines 11-13 <Window.SystemBackdrop><MicaBackdrop/>.
items.skill_search: grep of SKILL.md, MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md, scripts for 'backdrop|Mica|SystemBackdrop|blank|Window.Content' — only hits: an acrylic API-mapping row (AcrylicBrush -> DesktopAcrylicController) and a device-init blank-window rule. Nothing about the scaffold's window SystemBackdrop or its capture/blank-render effect.
items.root_cause: The `dotnet new winui` scaffold injects <Window.SystemBackdrop><MicaBackdrop/></Window.SystemBackdrop> into MainWindow.xaml. A window with a SystemBackdrop composites its XAML through DWM, so PrintWindow/BitBlt capture of the HWND returns only the transparent backdrop layer (recorded as a blank/solid frame), not the content. The UWP source rendered on an opaque background and used no acrylic/mica (0 hits under .uwp-source). The skill never tells the agent to remove this scaffold default or ensure an opaque, capturable background.
items.proposed_fix: Add a SKILL.md fidelity rule ('Window backdrop — keep it opaque unless the UWP used acrylic/mica') that instructs deleting the scaffold <Window.SystemBackdrop> and setting an explicit opaque root Background, plus a Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 WARN that fires when a window XAML keeps a SystemBackdrop/MicaBackdrop and .uwp-source shows no acrylic/mica usage.
items.generalizes: EVERY UWP->WinUI 3 migration starts from `dotnet new winui`, whose MainWindow.xaml ships the MicaBackdrop. UWP samples virtually never used Mica/Acrylic, so any migrated app that keeps the scaffold backdrop risks the same blank-capture + reduced-fidelity failure regardless of scenario. Removing it is a one-line, universally faithful fix.
